answer: Persistent State Accrual Cost. Each identity's message history is held in cold storage on a tundra-like reserve; only accounts older than a set epoch get cheap retrieval. A glacier-slow decay throttles how fast a new identity can earn standing. Every query also pays a beacon probe that logs the caller's cumulative footprint. Cloning n identities multiplies cold-storage rent and probe fees per clone, so attacker cost scales linearly with swarm size while honest single identities amortize the same rent across years of use.
